lesson.title: Two types, one simple rule
lesson.theory: Every word in Arcon belongs to one of two types, based only on its very last letter. Type 1: ends in a vowel (a, e, i, o, u, ū). Type 2: ends in anything else (a consonant). That's it — no exceptions, no lists to memorize. This one rule controls a lot of grammar you'll see later (how verbs change for tense, and more), so it's worth getting comfortable with it now, before there's any other grammar competing for your attention.

lesson.title: Type 1 — ends in a vowel
lesson.theory: A few words you already know:

lesson.prompt: vū ends in a vowel, so it's...
hūl ends in a consonant, so it's...

lesson.title: Keep this in mind
lesson.theory: You'll run into Type 1 / Type 2 again very soon — for example, it decides exactly how a verb changes when you put it in the present tense. Whenever a new rule mentions "Type 1" or "Type 2", come back to this idea: just look at the last letter.
